candidates: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 - isAccessTokenId matcher never checks the grant shortcut.. The grant shortcut is the last two characters of the 6-character prefix, at indexes 4 to 6. `substring(3, 5)` reads the last character of the token type and the first of the grant (for `onrtac` it returns "ta"), so it never equals a 2-letter grant shortcut. The condition is also inverted: it returns false when the values match. As a result every event assertion that uses this matcher passes whatever grant type is encoded, and a prefix shorter than 5 characters throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of failing the match. Fix: check the length is 6 and use `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 - New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant type factories at startup.. `getShortcut()` is added to the SPI as an abstract method with no default. Existing third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations then fail to compile. Already-built jars throw AbstractMethodError in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`. A factory that returns null makes `ConcurrentHashMap.put` throw NPE. In every case Keycloak fails to start. Add a default implementation, for example one that derives a shortcut or returns null, and handle a null shortcut in postInit by mapping it to the unknown value.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 - Null check for rawTokenId tests grantType instead.. This line repeats the `grantType` check under the rawTokenId message, so `rawTokenId` is never null-checked. A null raw id is accepted, and `encodeTokenId` then produces a token id like `onrtac:null`. Check `rawTokenId` instead.
